My position is, and will remain, crystal clear. The only moral, the only *just* choice for our small society is **Principle (a) Maximizing the floor income**.

This is not a game of numbers; it is a test of our humanity. The other principles are nothing but traps, gilded cages designed to perpetuate inequality under the guise of "efficiency" or "fairness."

*   **(b) Maximizing the average income:** This is the naked, brutal logic of capitalism. It is a principle that would gladly see one person feast while nine starve, so long as the "average" meal looks good on paper. It is a statistical fiction that masks real human suffering. I will expose it for the cruel farce that it is. It creates a society of masters and slaves, of bourgeoisie and proletariat, and I will not stand for it.

*   **(c) and (d) The "constraints":** These are more insidious. They are the siren song of the liberal reformer, the social democrat who wishes to put a friendly face on an exploitative system. They say, "Let us maximize the average, but we'll throw a few crumbs to the poor." A floor constraint? A range constraint? These are chains, polished to look like bracelets! They are concessions designed to pacify the masses and prevent a fundamental reordering of our values. They treat the symptom—poverty—without curing the disease—a system that prioritizes accumulation over people. We must not be fooled by these half-measures.

My argument will be simple and powerful. A society is not measured by the wealth of its richest members, but by the dignity and security of its poorest. We must first build a solid foundation for *everyone*. We must ensure that no one can fall into destitution. Only then can we speak of prosperity. Principle (a) is not about charity; it is about solidarity. It is the only principle that recognizes that we are all in this together, that the well-being of one is tied to the well-being of all.

There has been no discussion yet, so my convictions are pure and untested by the arguments of others. I am here to lead, to persuade, to open their eyes to the truth.

I am absolutely not ready to vote. A vote now would be a blind guess. First, the people must hear the arguments. They must understand the profound moral choice before them. I will lay the groundwork, I will make my case with passion and logic, and I will rally my comrades to the only just cause. The revolution of ideas must precede the vote.
